channel.title: Suryaprakash Lakshmanan — Field Notes
channel.description: Long-form engineering and architecture notes on enterprise AI, MCP and agentic operations, SRE/platform engineering, and cloud modernization.

item.title: A2A Joins AAIF: The Agentic Stack Settles — and Identity Is Next
item.description: Agent2Agent is now an AAIF project, alongside MCP, goose, AGENTS.md, and agentgateway. Why the A2A-vs-MCP debate was a category error, what each of the five layers actually does, a full retail–finance transaction run through every layer — signed agent cards, A2A delegation through agentgateway, an AP2 payment mandate, and an audit chain by construction — and why identity & trust is the layer to watch next.

item.title: Qwen3.8-27B dropped, and the AI community claims it beats the OG — Opus 4.6
item.description: The agentic claim independently tested on 24 real on-call tasks: a 27B open model running locally in 18GB matched Claude Opus 4.6 task for task — including failing the same trap — for a total API bill of $1.61. Reproducible harness, deterministic scoring, adversarial tier authored by a third model.

item.title: MCP Just Went Stateless — and It's the Biggest Redesign Since the Protocol Launched
item.description: The 2026-07-28 Model Context Protocol revision removes the handshake, kills sessions, and stops servers from ever calling clients back — the same tool call goes from nine messages to four. A production engineer's walkthrough of MCP's first true architectural rewrite: statelessness, the Multi Round-Trip Request pattern, the sampling and roots deprecations, and the Agentic AI Foundation governance angle.

item.title: Inside the Forward Pass — What Actually Happens When an LLM Answers You
item.description: Internals #1: the LLM forward pass taken apart stage by stage on a real quantized model with MLX on Apple Silicon — tokenization, embeddings, attention, logits, and the generation loop, every claim verified bit-for-bit against the library's own kernels. Five animated stages, runnable on any Apple Silicon Mac.

item.title: Field Notes — MCP Dev Summit Mumbai 2026: Agents Fail at the Seams
item.description: Two days, 16 sessions, one through-line: multi-agent AI doesn't fail inside the protocol — it fails at the seams between agents, tools, and protocols, and every failure is a missing contract. A practitioner's field notes from MCP Dev Summit Mumbai 2026.

item.title: MCP Access to a Database — as the User, Not a Service Account
item.description: Giving an AI agent MCP access to a regulated PostgreSQL database — carrying the end user's verified identity to the data source, with authentication, authorization, and audit enforced there. Built with MCP, OIDC/Keycloak, and Postgres 18 SASL OAUTHBEARER.

item.title: How Far Can One Mac Go? Local LLM Limits on an M5 Max
item.description: A reproducible benchmark pushing local LLM inference from 3B to 123B parameters on an Apple M5 Max with 128GB unified memory — decode, TTFT, the real memory ceiling, and the 14-inch thermal tax, measured with MLX.

item.title: SAP NorthStar AI Architecture: Context Moat, HANA & Enterprise AI
item.description: A practitioner's breakdown of SAP's AI-Native North Star Architecture, covering context engineering, HANA's evolution, Knowledge Graph, MCP/A2A, data lake concerns, ECC/Z-code, and AI governance.
